heading_en: Positioning of Consecutive Opening Brackets, Closing Brackets, Commas, Full Stops and Middle Dots
heading_ja: 始め括弧類，終わり括弧類，読点類，句点類及び​中点類が​連続する​場合の​配置方法

cases.quote: In cases where multiple punctuation marks, such as opening brackets (cl-01), closing brackets (cl-02), commas (cl-07), full stops (cl-06) and middle dots (cl-05), come one after the other, the following spacing adjustments are made for aesthetic reasons (see Figure 69).
cases.rationale: The rule's own plainest instance of two punctuation marks coming one after the other: a closing bracket (cl-02) immediately followed by an opening bracket (cl-01), the ）（ of two adjacent parenthetical remarks Figure 69 draws. Table 1's own cell at this coordinate reads `1/2 be` (`spec/captured/table1.en.tsv`'s own row for cl-02/cl-01), and `crates/jlreq-spacing/src/generated/table1.rs` cites it to the generic `RuleId::SPACING_BETWEEN_CHARACTERS` rather than to a numbered note — checked directly against the generated cell at `before: 2, after: 1` — because this coordinate carries no note of its own anywhere in Appendix B; the same unnoted shape `B/opening-bracket-then-middle-dot/an-unnoted-cell-cites-appendix-bs-own-sentence` already reads at a different pair. This case reads the identical unnoted cell for §3.1.4's own first sentence instead, which is the sentence this document's own words assign the coordinate to even though no generated table cell cites this address by name anywhere in the crate (checked by grep across `crates/jlreq-spacing/src/generated/`, matching what `3.1.9/full-stop-at-line-end/table-4-alone-stays-rigid-among-the-three`'s own rationale already establishes for a different address sharing a Table 1 cell with §D.1's own generic legend citation): coverage in this suite is counted per address, not per citation a generated cell happens to carry. `crates/jlreq-spacing/src/space.rs`'s own `Referent` doc is the linchpin this case turns on — "Every note that assigns a conditional space assigns owner and referent together — 'the conditional half em space accompanying the preceding comma' — so this is one concept and one field" — and Appendix B's own `be`/`af` legend is exactly that: a lone `be` token names one owner, the preceding character, and states nothing about the trailing one. `1/2 be` at cl-02 x cl-01 is therefore the closing bracket's own half em and nothing contributed by the opening bracket that follows it, the identical reading `D.2/full-stop-then-middle-dot/the-full-stops-half-em-never-reduces` and `B.2/full-stop-then-middle-dot/the-unadjusted-sum-of-a-half-em-and-a-quarter-em` already establish at cl-06 x cl-05 for a `be`-only cell of their own. Under the declared default (Table 3) the half em is in fact reducible, at the fifth priority, to a zero floor — `1/2-0 stage 5` in `spec/captured/table3.en.tsv`'s own row for cl-02/cl-01 — which this case's one `permitted` entry states plainly because the point here is the shape of the amount (one conditional space, owned by the preceding character) and not which table drains it; that second question is `3.1.4/comma-then-opening-bracket/the-half-em-is-subject-to-line-adjustment`'s own subject, at the coordinate sentence 2 names.

permitted.source: JLReq §3.1.4, Table 3 (JLReq's own adopted method, §D preamble)

forbidden.why: Table 1's own `be` token names the preceding character's own em and nothing about the trailing one, exactly as `crates/jlreq-spacing/src/space.rs`'s own `Referent` doc states: 'the conditional half em space accompanying the preceding comma' is one concept and one field. Reading `1/2 be` at cl-02 x cl-01 as a space owned by the trailing opening bracket confuses 'the space that sits before the opening bracket, read from the opening bracket's own side' with what the note actually assigns, which is the closing bracket's own contribution. Nothing in this cell or in §3.1.4's own text gives the opening bracket (cl-01) a conditional space of its own at this boundary.

cases.quote: Note also that the half em and quarter em spacing added before or after punctuation marks, including the half em spacing after full stops (cl-06) appearing in the middle of a line, are subject, in principle, to line adjustment and may eventually be removed, except for those added after full stops (cl-06).
cases.rationale: The positive control for sentence 2's general rule, read at a comma (cl-07) rather than at the closing bracket the case above reads, so this case also demonstrates that the rule's list of five punctuation classes is not read as a single undifferentiated pair: Table 1's cell at cl-07/cl-01 carries the identical token cl-02/cl-01 carries, `1/2 be` (`spec/captured/table1.en.tsv`), because a comma and a closing bracket share one half-em contribution at this position (§3.1.2's own advance rule over both). The Japanese half of sentence 2 states the rule this case is the positive half of precisely: 「行中における句点類（cl-06）の後ろの二分アキを除いて」，原則として二分アキ又は四分アキとする箇所は，行の調整処理の詰める場合の対象にしてよい — every half or quarter em this document adds before or after a punctuation mark may, in principle, be drained by line adjustment, with one stated exception. A comma's own half em is not that exception, so all three reduction matrices open a real, continuous opportunity to drain it: `spec/captured/table3.en.tsv` reads `1/2-0 stage 5` at cl-07/cl-01, `table4.en.tsv` reads `1/2-0 stage 3`, and `table5.en.tsv` reads `1/2-1/4 stage 3` — a dash in every one of the three, which `xtask/src/spacing.rs`'s own `ranged_cell` (`(None, Some((amount, limit))) => (amount, Some(limit), false)`) and `crates/jlreq-spacing/src/evaluate.rs`'s own `cell_reduction` (`Some(floor) if cell.two_valued => Reduction::Discrete`, else `Range`) both read as `Reduction::Range`, continuously shrinking, never the two-valued `Discrete` §3.1.9 reserves for a different boundary — the run of this suite selects only the Table 3 entry under the declared default (`crates/jlreq-conform/src/run.rs`'s own `applicable()`, `Kumihan::default()` declaring `Policy::JLREQ` whose own default answer to `adjustment.reduction_table` is `table-3`), so the Table 4 and Table 5 entries below are statements to an implementation that declares those alternatives, never the applicable entry this run measures — the identical scope limit `D.2/two-middle-dots/quarter-em-each-side-reduces-at-a-different-stage-per-table`'s own entry above already states for the same axis.

permitted.source: JLReq §3.1.4 sentence 2, Table 3 (JLReq's own adopted method, §D preamble)
JLReq §3.1.4 sentence 2, Table 4 (JIS X 4051's alternative, §D preamble)
JLReq §3.1.4 sentence 2, Table 5 (a third method found in other publications, §D preamble)

forbidden.why: §3.1.9's own two-valued restriction — 'the possibilities are only half em spacing or solid' — is stated over the closing-bracket, full-stop and comma spacing at the line end, a different boundary from this one; this case's own coordinate is interior, one comma followed immediately by one opening bracket, mid-line. None of the three permitted entries above answers `discrete` at this coordinate: `spec/captured/table3.en.tsv`'s own `1/2-0 stage 5` cell carries a dash, not an equals sign, and `crates/jlreq-spacing/src/evaluate.rs`'s own `cell_reduction` reads a dash as `Reduction::Range` and reserves `Reduction::Discrete` for the equals-sign token `D.1/closing-bracket-at-line-end/table-4-protects-what-table-3-and-5-drain`'s own `1/2=0 stage 2` cell carries at the line end instead. Reading this interior comma-then-bracket boundary as two-valued imports §3.1.9's own line-end shape onto a coordinate that sentence does not state it for.

cases.quote: Note also that the half em and quarter em spacing added before or after punctuation marks, including the half em spacing after full stops (cl-06) appearing in the middle of a line, are subject, in principle, to line adjustment and may eventually be removed, except for those added after full stops (cl-06).
cases.rationale: The exception sentence 2 states in its own second half, at the one coordinate this rule generalizes and the round exists for: a full stop (cl-06) immediately followed by an opening bracket (cl-01). Table 1's cell here reads `1/2 be` (`spec/captured/table1.en.tsv`'s own row for cl-06/cl-01), the identical token the two cases above read at cl-02/cl-01 and cl-07/cl-01 — the amount does not distinguish the full stop from the other two classes at all. What distinguishes it is §3.1.4's own text, in both renderings, though the two renderings do not agree on where the exception reaches. The English half reads: 'the half em and quarter em spacing added before or after punctuation marks, including the half em spacing after full stops (cl-06) appearing in the middle of a line, are subject, in principle, to line adjustment and may eventually be removed, except for those added after full stops (cl-06)' — which first states, in so many words, that a full stop's mid-line half em *is* included among the spaces subject to line adjustment, and then excepts everything added after a full stop, contradicting the clause six words earlier within the same sentence, and states no 行末 (line-end) qualifier of any kind. The Japanese half reads the opposite shape and is internally consistent: 「なお，行中における句点類（cl-06）の後ろの二分アキを除いて，行末における句点類（cl-06）の後ろの二分アキを含めて原則として二分アキ又は四分アキとする箇所は，行の調整処理の詰める場合の対象にしてよい」 — excluding, from the places that may in principle be drained by line adjustment, the half em after a full stop appearing *mid-line* (行中), while including the half em after a full stop *at the line end* (行末) among them. This case's own coordinate is squarely the mid-line one both halves agree is excepted (the exception is what the English half also states, once its own six-words-earlier clause is set aside as the internal contradiction it is), so the two renderings converge on the same answer here even though they diverge over the line-end reading §3.1.9 and §B.2 note 6 separately govern. This project's own established treatment is to read the half that states the qualifier: `spec/derived/defects.tsv`'s own `d2-note-5-line-end-qualifier-omitted-in-english` entry records the identical shape of divergence one note over — its own English half 'states no position' where its Japanese half names 行末に配置する — and its own `treatment` column resolves it in exactly these words: 'The role of the position is read from the Japanese half, which is the half that states it, exactly as the two other locale divergences are.' `spec/derived/defects.tsv` was searched directly for `3.1.4` before writing this rationale and returns no entry; this divergence is new to that ledger and is named here, precisely enough for a follow-up round to add it under `xtask/src/defects.rs`'s own machine-verified `evidence` predicates, rather than re-derived. The three captured reduction matrices corroborate the Japanese reading independently, at both of its coordinates: at this case's own mid-line coordinate, cl-06/cl-01, every one of Table 3, Table 4 and Table 5 reads a bare `1/2` (`spec/captured/table3.en.tsv`, `table4.en.tsv` and `table5.en.tsv`'s own rows), no dash, no equals sign, no stage — the full stop's own half em is rigid under all three tables at once, unlike the comma's and the closing bracket's identical-looking `1/2 be` two cases above, which every one of the three tables opens a real reduction opportunity for. At the line-end coordinate the same divergence resurfaces in exactly the shape §D.2 note 5's own defect predicts: `table3.en.tsv` reads `1/2=0 stage 2` for cl-06/line-end (a real, if discrete, reduction — the Japanese half's 行末…を含めて) while `table4.en.tsv` reads a bare `1/2`, rigid — matching neither the English half's stated inclusion nor a uniform rigidity, and settled instead by `3.1.9/full-stop-at-line-end/table-4-alone-stays-rigid-among-the-three`'s own case, which is this rule's own cross-referenced address (§3.1.9) and outside this case's scope. `standing` is `normative` rather than `adjudicated` because the three reduction matrices are unanimous at this case's own coordinate: publishing all three below is a statement about that unanimity, not about two permitted readings a policy could select between, and `adjudicated` would wrongly imply a second reading belongs under `permitted` that nothing in the policy space selects.

permitted.source: JLReq §3.1.4 sentence 2's own exception, Table 3 (JLReq's own adopted method, §D preamble) — unanimous with Table 4 and Table 5 at this coordinate
JLReq §3.1.4 sentence 2's own exception, Table 4 (JIS X 4051's alternative, §D preamble) — the same rigid reading
JLReq §3.1.4 sentence 2's own exception, Table 5 (a third method found in other publications, §D preamble) — the same rigid reading again

forbidden.why: This is `3.1.4/comma-then-opening-bracket/the-half-em-is-subject-to-line-adjustment`'s own Table 3 answer at cl-07/cl-01, read onto this case's cl-06/cl-01 coordinate instead. §3.1.4 sentence 2 names the full stop's own half em, and only the full stop's, as the one exception to the general reducibility the comma's identical-looking half em is subject to; none of the three captured reduction matrices reads a dash or a stage number at cl-06/cl-01 — every one reads a bare `1/2` — so answering this coordinate as reducible treats the full stop's own contribution as though it were the comma's or the closing bracket's, which §3.1.4's own text is careful to except by name.
